subject: Host assertion & cert delegation for on-prem private hostname
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@acme-analytics.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: infraops@acme-analytics.com, mike.lee@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-01-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private hostname validation & cert handoff for on-prem Edge

Hi Olga,

We're kicking off the private deployment pilot for Acme Analytics and want to align on how Redwood will assert ownership of our on-prem hostname (edge.acme.internal) and how TLS termination will be handled. Our security team prefers we avoid sharing private keys; they asked about options for either:

- DNS-based proof (zone delegation or TXT proof) so Redwood can obtain certs, or
- Or an offline CSR workflow where we generate the key on our side and hand you a CSR to sign, or
- Using our internal CA/ACME runner with a trust bundle distribution.

Can you outline recommended approaches, what we (Acme) will need to provide, and any required timeline? Also include what telemetry/logs Redwood will collect for compliance.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Nguyen
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics

Attachments: none
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private hostname validation & cert handoff for on-prem Edge

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. I sketched two production-safe patterns we recommend for private-hosted endpoints and the tradeoffs: see inline.

Option A — Delegated DNS (preferred when customer controls DNS)
- Customer creates a zone delegation (NS) for the edge FQDN (or a subzone) to our validation nameservers, or alternatively allows TXT-based ACME validation records mounted via your DNS provider API.
- Redwood uses ACME DNS-01 to mint short-lived certificates (7–30 day TTL) and rotates automatically.
- Customer never shares private keys; Redwood retains certs in our HSM-backed store.
- Requirements from Acme: ability to create the TXT records or set the NS delegation; a contact for DNS ops; an allowlist for our validation IPs.
- Pros: automated renewals, minimal manual handoffs. Cons: requires DNS change/automation access.

Option B — Offline CSR (preferred when customer cannot delegate DNS)
- Acme generates the private key on-prem and produces a CSR (we provide csr-template.txt).
- Customer uploads signed CSR via secure upload (S3/transfer appliance) or we accept via mutual TLS established management channel. Redwood signs the CSR with our intermediate that is trusted by Redwood runtime, or alternatively we return a CSR-signed cert that you install behind your ingress.
- We can optionally generate a cert signed by your CA if you provide signing access via an on-prem ACME runner (we can integrate).
- Requirements from Acme: signed CSR, installation steps, certificate install automation (optional).
- Pros: customer retains key control. Cons: manual renewals unless ACME runner is available.

Additional controls we will apply regardless of approach:
- OCSP stapling and short cert lifetimes for private endpoints; mandatory OCSP responder configs when using Redwood-signed certs.
- Audit logs of issuance + rotation events (we can provide redacted issuance evidence for compliance).
- Ability to pin to a customer-provided trust bundle for mutual-TLS client validation if requested.

Next steps I propose:
1) Choose preferred option (A or B) for edge.acme.internal.
2) If A, provide DNS contact + ability to create TXT/NS records; we'll send list of validation record names and IPs.
3) If B, confirm secure upload destination and we will share csr-template.txt and example installation steps.
4) Kick off a 60-minute sync to review the automation path and compliance artifacts.

I've attached a short checklist that covers required fields and timelines. Happy to review with your InfraOps team.

–Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ownership-checklist.pdf, csr-template.txt
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Sara Nguyen <sara@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-18T14:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private hostname validation & cert handoff for on-prem Edge

Sara/Olga — quick technical notes from the runtime side (this is a short list of gotchas we've seen on similar on-prem pilots):

- If you go with Delegated DNS + ACME: prefer TXT validation over HTTP-01 for private namespaces. Ensure TTLs are low during cutover so validation records propagate quickly.
- For Offline CSR: recommend a 2-week rolling overlap window during the first rotation to validate install automation; include a health-check endpoint for cert presence.
- For mutual trust: we distribute a Redwood intermediate by default. If Acme wants us to trust their internal CA, we will accept a PEM bundle and run an internal validation job to ensure the chain. Note: if you supply a customer CA chain, OCSP responder semantics differ — we will require an OCSP responder URI or stapling will be disabled.
- SNI mapping: if you host many tenant-specific private FQDNs behind the same egress, we'll need a canonicalization table (FQDN -> tenant id). Please provide the initial mapping in CSV format.
- Vault/Provisioning: we recommend storing customer-provided CA bundles in our HSM-backed Vault and providing a delivery token scoped to the customer's Dedicated environment.

I'll be available on the sync and can run through a checklist of automation scripts we can hand over.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-21T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private hostname validation & cert handoff for on-prem Edge

Sara — thanks, that all sounds good. After reviewing security requirements with our compliance lead, Acme's security team authorized Option A (Delegated DNS with TXT validation) for the pilot, with a fallback to Option B (offline CSR) if delegation proves infeasible.

Requested next steps:
- Acme InfraOps to create a subzone (edge.acme.internal) delegation to the validation nameservers we'll send you. If delegation is not allowed, please upload the first CSR by 2026-02-01.
- Acme to share a primary DNS contact + maintenance window for the initial validation (we prefer a 1-hour window during week of Feb 1).
- Redwood will provide the validation record names, a short-lived cert policy doc, and an evidence export format for audit.

Can Infra Ops please reply-all to confirm the delegation window? Olga/Karthik — please prepare the validation nameserver IP list and the TXT names by EOD Monday.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions & Compliance, Redwood Inference
